EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the hallmark anhydride carbonyl doublet with strong bands at ~1795 and ~1875 cm⁻¹, consistent with cyclic anhydrides (symmetric/antisymmetric ν(C=O)). Candidate 1 is a chlorinated maleic anhydride derivative, matching this pattern and the strong C=C band at 1624 cm⁻¹ (alkene). The very intense 649 cm⁻¹ band fits a C–Cl stretching region (see GFQ-046), which candidate 1 uniquely provides among the anhydrides here. Additional bands at 1213/1256 cm⁻¹ are compatible with anhydride C–O stretches, and features near 893/935 cm⁻¹ plausibly arise from C–O–C ring modes. Other candidates either lack an anhydride (thus cannot explain the carbonyl doublet) or lack chlorine (thus cannot explain the dominant 649 cm⁻¹ band).
